notes.title: Patch 2018.0905 Notes
notes.notes:
I've just released the first update for PSF 2019, based on feedback from users.

Update 2018.0905 (Sept 5, 2018)
If your career has a problem from the initial version, you should either simulate the entire current season or start with a new career.  However, I don't expect you to have any problems.

Fixes:
- several fixes to Career play when coaching or simulating individual games
- now correctly update Career History all the time
- now automatically advance to offseason when simulating super bowl
- fix display of divisions to vary by conference
- fixed OT rules for regular season and playoffs

Enhancements:
- Can now switch image sets on existing career!
- Can now switch image sets on the fly!
- Analyze Game now displays Point Spread (desktop versions)
- Default End Zones now use all caps on team name and nickname
- several cosmetic changes

notes.title: Calling Plays
notes.notes:
Someone here asked a great question about calling plays.  With PSF you can quickly simulate games or even seasons, and you can even watch a game played out between two computer coaches.

But there's incredible power and fun in the coaching side, too!  In fact, I love that aspect of football (and because I love playing my brother).  Just set the coach to Player 1 or Player 2 (rather than Computer).  Now, some caveats.

Most important, there are two game levels - Beginner and Expert.  Beginner is great fun and fast, but you're basically leaning over to your coordinator and calling "run off tackle" or "throw short" (or "defend inside runs"), and then your coordinator sets the details.

But now, if you want full bore control, select Expert.  Now you can do something like this:
1) Counter Left
2) with the HB (or FB)
3) from the Pro I (or any of 12 formations)
4) strong right or strong left
5) tap any flanker and send him in motion

or on a pass play, tell your FB to stay in and block, and set the passing routes of every receiver.  AND see at a glance every receiver's ratings and game stats.

Defense is the same.  Beginner is easier and great for fast games.  But in Expert mode, you can
1) focus on Run or Pass
2) call your formation (4-3, 3-4, Nickel, Dime, etc)
3) shift your line, if four man (stunt, over, under, tight, wide, normal)
4) call your coverage (man, 2-deep, 3-deep)
5) set your run keys (normal, key on flow, key on a man)
6) if in pass defense, double a receiver

And in blitz, you can easily blitz any linebacker(s).  Maybe send the LILB and RILB to stuff the inside, or just your ROLB, etc.

And again, you can see all the receiver's ratings and stats, so you'll know which man is most dangerous.

One more thing, be sure to click all the buttons, because you also have access to:
1) clock management
2) a playbook where you can save your ten favorite plays
3) reports (situation, previous play, game stats, injuries, achievements, scouting)
4) current game highlights reel
5) AND VERY IMPORTANT - the coach icon in the lower left.  The AI can give you advice or even suggest a play for you.

And you can switch between Beginner and Expert at any time.

Enjoy!

notes.title: Home Field Advantage
notes.notes:
You can turn this off in Settings, but I wanted to let you know that in PSF, homefield advantage is roughly three points.

To test it out, I had the Rams at the Chargers and ran 1000 simulations multiple times, and got either a tie (most often) or a one point spread.

Then I switched and had the Chargers visit at the Rams (Rams now have homefield advantage), and each time, the point spread wound up being Rambs by three.

notes.title: Tweaking Teams
notes.notes:
I thought I'd share something I've done recently, so it might spur your own creativity.

Editing leagues involves converting to and from CSV files (easily editable in Excel or any spreadsheet editor).
 league <---> csv file

So, I would edit the csv file, which was in the "import_export" folder, tweaking a team or two.  Then in the game, I would import the csv file and overwrite the league I was testing.

Then I headed to Single Season play and simulated the 2018 season several times (very fast on my desktop!).  If I thought something needed tweaking, or if I was just curious (what if I change this team to pass a little more?), I could change the csv file, import, etc.

Very fast!

Oh, and in career play, you can edit each year's draft pool!

notes.title: Customizing PSF 2019
notes.notes:
I've implemented Steam Cloud, which is very handy for keeping your customizations and saved games, etc across machines.  However, I haven't had time to implement Steam Workshop yet.

So, I wanted to briefly explain how you'll customize PSF 2019 within Windows and MacOS.

At a high level, it's simply a matter of sharing leagues (binary files) and image sets (folders).  Your game has three subfolders under it, and the game will tell you the path when you click on the "Customizing PSF" button.  The folders are:
[list]
    [*]leagues (every league there is available to your game, just paste new ones there)
    [*]import_export (more on that later)
    [*]images (here is where you'll create subfolders)
[/list]

So, the game will already have
[list]
    [*]leagues
            2019_leagues.lgs
    [*]import_export
            2019_leagues.csv
    [*]images
           default/  (don't change these, you'll lose your changes)
[/list]

and you might add, say a set of real nfl images and another set of real college images, and maybe a set of fantasy images (orcs, elves, etc).  Heck, maybe a sci-fi set, you get the idea.

Each of those would go in a folder under "images" so now your game folder looks like this:

psf2019
[list]
    [*]leagues
        [list]
        [*]2019_leagues.lgs
        [*]2019_real_nfl_names.lgs
        [*]lotro_players.lgs
        [/list]
    [*]import_export
        [list]
        [*]2019_leagues.csv 
        [/list]
    [*]images
        [list]
        [*]real_nfl/ 
        [*]1977_images/ 
        [*]lotro/ 
        [*]scifi/ 
        [/list]
[/list]

and at any time, you can launch the "mini editor" for a league and change the name of its images folder, and it immediately starts using those images!

notes.title: Watch or Coach All Teams now, in Career Play!
notes.notes:
I finished this feature after creating the video.  A lot of people have requested the option to watch or coach all teams and games in career play.  I'm happy to say that I've now implemented that!

In addition, some folks asked me to improve "watch a simulation" by getting rid of all pausing (penalty screens, injuries, scoring summaries, ends of quarters, etc), and I've done that as well!

In addition, you can now change your team's game plan at any point in the season, and can even tweak it for individual games!
